what: The entropy deciders' arithmetic checked against Arb (python-flint): instruments/bigfloat as instruments/sumdiff and instruments/optq/twolaw.js call it, and the Python standard library's decimal as tools/verify_sumdiff.py, tools/verify_twolaw.py and instruments/fei/fei.py call it, each run through its REAL functions on seeded random and adversarial inputs and on the registry's own certificates; every enclosure required to contain the exact value, decided in Arb at 256 bits and up from the exact inputs (exactly, in FLINT's rationals, when the value is rational); every malformed input required to be refused; planted wrong functions required to be caught. Written by tools/audit-entropy-arb.js with tools/audit-entropy-arb.py.

implPrecision.bigfloat: bits per case (u.b): 128, 256, 512, 1024 as sumdiff/twolaw escalate; ln2 also 24..4096

beyondTheDoor: bf.plnp>1 and py.plnp>1 feed the bare -p ln p routines a p > 1, which no door admits (sumdiff.door, verify_sumdiff.read and verify_twolaw.laws require a law summing to 1). They are a measurement of how load-bearing the door is, not a requirement: verify_sumdiff.entropy takes p_lo·(−ln_hi) as its lower end, which holds only while −ln p >= 0.

foundAtPin.what: The findings this audit made at its first full run, recorded in certs/entropy-arb-audit.json at the commit named, before any fix (the gaps recorded at the pin), with the digests of the modules audited then; each was fixed afterwards in the file named. The audit's declared list (KNOWN in tools/audit-entropy-arb.py) is now empty: any one of these reproducing again fails the run.

findings.name: decide()["H"]
findings.why: fei.decide returns its enclosures as strings cut from str(): ratio [str(r_lo)[:44], str(r_hi)[:44]] and H [str(H_lo)[:30], str(H_hi)[:30]]. Cutting a decimal string rounds toward zero — for a positive upper end, DOWN — so the returned upper end falls below the exact value whenever the cut drops a nonzero digit. The verdict is not affected: decide() compares the full 60-digit r_lo with the threshold, and the full-precision ends (fei.H, fei.ratio) contain the value.
findings.fixedIn: instruments/fei/fei.py: outward(x, digits, up) prints the lower end rounded down and the upper end up (ROUND_FLOOR / ROUND_CEILING) at 43 (ratio) and 29 (H) significant digits

The verdict is not affected: decide() compares the full 60-digit r_lo with the threshold, and the full-precision ends (fei.H, fei.ratio) contain the value.

findings.name: verify_sumdiff: a non-integer weight that truncates to a law (num 1.9/2 and 1.2/2)
findings.why: read() applies int() to JSON numbers (1.9 -> 1, 1.2 -> 1), so a certificate whose weights are not integers is decided as the law {1/2, 1/2}; sumdiff.js refuses it.
findings.fixedIn: tools/verify_sumdiff.py: law() refuses a coordinate or weight that is not an exact integer (a JSON float or a boolean) and a one-point law (every entropy 0, the ratio 0/0); ratio() refuses when the maximum entropy is not separated from 0; each with its reason
